output.question: Has T-Mobile announced layoffs?
output.answer: Yes. T-Mobile US has been cutting jobs under a "2025-2026 workforce transformation" restructuring that began in Q4 2025. In an SEC filing, parent company Deutsche Telekom reported 4,671 fewer positions at T-Mobile US in the first half of 2026: headcount fell from 70,036 at the end of 2025 to 65,365 by mid-2026, a drop of 6.7%. In late August 2026, T-Mobile also filed a WARN notice in Washington state for 63 new layoffs across 13 locations, covering retail stores and its headquarters, scheduled between September 21 and November 18, 2026. Six stores are closing as part of that notice.

key_facts.fact: Deutsche Telekom reported in an SEC filing that T-Mobile US cut 4,671 positions in H1 2026 because of 'the impact of the 2025-2026 workforce transformation'.
T-Mobile US headcount went from 70,036 at end-2025 to 65,365 at mid-2026, a 6.7% decline.
The workforce transformation began in Q4 2025. It streamlines operations by centralizing leaders and teams and cutting organizational layers.

T-Mobile filed notice with Washington's Employment Security Department of 63 new layoffs across 13 locations (retail stores and HQ), set for Sept 21 to Nov 18, 2026. Another 14 previously announced layoffs were deferred into the same window.
Six Washington locations are closing: Seattle, Bellingham, Bothell, Vancouver, Kennewick and Tacoma. Some employees were offered relocation.

passages.quote: the impact of the 2025-2026 workforce transformation
The telco workforce has been shrinking for years due mainly to automation, not AI

caveats: The 4,671 figure is a net drop in headcount reported by Deutsche Telekom. It is not a single layoff announcement, and some of the change may come from attrition or integrating acquired companies (UScellular, Metronet, Lumos, USI).

I could not open the primary T-Mobile Q3 2026 10-Q's restructuring note (Note 15). A search snippet said severance costs reached $531M as of Sept 30, 2026, with the remaining separations expected through 2026, but I did not confirm this on the filing page.
Layoff trackers give different counts for the August 2026 Washington WARN notice (77 vs. a revised 159). The Fast Company/Yahoo article reports 63 new layoffs plus 14 deferred ones.
Only SDxCentral's paraphrase is available for the Deutsche Telekom filing; I did not open the filing itself. The Fierce Network article returned a 403 error.
I found no layoff announcements after August 2026 as of 2026-11-11, but the search may not have caught every recent WARN filing.
